RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the December 11, 2008/Agrahayana 20, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North Eastern Region;
Environment and Forests; External Affairs; Housing and
Urban Poverty Alleviation; Information and Broadcasting;
Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj; Parliamentary
Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions;
Planning; Shipping, Road Transport and Highways;
Space; Statistics and Programme Implementation;
Urban Development; Y outh Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
49
3G spectrum bids
*141. SHRI VIJAY JAW AHARLAL
DARDA:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry  has delayed
3G spectrum bids considerably;
(b) if so, whether  the Ministry of
Finance has also urged his Ministry to hold
auction  as early as possible so that the
estimated Rs. 40,000 crores can be
budgeted in the current fiscal books to
bridge the fiscal deficit;
(c) if so, whether  a number of political
parties have also criticised Government over
the favouring of chosen corporates;
(d) if so, whether  the new 3G telecom
is to share a 3 per cent  revenue with
Government; and
(e) if so, by what time a final decision in
this regard is likely to be taken?
Scheme for urban transport planning
*142. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government  is likely to
launch a Rs. 152 crore scheme for urban
transport planning to encourage States to
upgrade public transport systems which are
crumbling in most cities including the
Metros;
(b) if so, whether  his Ministry's
programme  that  is aimed at promoting  eco-
friendly, safe, comfortable and affordable
public transport would push cities to take
up  studies to prepare detailed project
reports after comprehensive and thorough
evaluation of alternate technologies;

50
(c) if so, whether his Ministry has
already started studies in this regard; and
(d) if so, by what time a final decision
in this regard is likely to be taken?
National  Urban Poor Fund
*143. SHRIMATI T. RA TNA BAI:
Will the Minister of HOUSING  AND
URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is setting up a
National Urban Poor Fund;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
purpose behind it;
(c) whether the master plans had
neglected the needs of the informal sector,
which engages 92 per cent of the total
workforce in cities and towns, especially
in the coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the steps to be taken in this
direction?
Dialogue with Foreign Minister of
Pakistan
*144. SHRIMATI  SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether  Foreign Ministers of India
and Pakistan met in May, 2008 to continue
the unfinished dialogue;
(b) if so, whether there was also a
meeting on Indo-Pak anti-terror mechanism
in the month of October, 2008;
(c) if so, the main subjects discussed
thereat;
(d) whether  any agreement in regard to
meeting the threat of terror has been reached;
(e) if so, to what extent  both countries
have implemented the proposals; and
(f) to what extent  anti-terror mechanism
of India and Pakistan has been successful?
Gap in consumption-expenditure
†*145. SHRI RAM JETH-
MALANI: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that  there is a
huge difference  in the consumption-
expenditure of the people living in the rural
and urban areas of the country;
(b) if so, the amount of monthly
expenditure on consumption, respectively,
by the people living in the rural and urban
areas during the years 2006 to 2008; and
(c) the details of this expenditure during
the years 1990 to 1992?
Funds for National Highway projects
*146. SHRI V . HANUMANTHA
RAO:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether in order to attract
companies to invest in Highway projects,
his Ministry has approached  the Finance
Ministry seeking low cost funds;
(b) whether  a special window from the
RBI that  would provide  for extension of
reasonable interest rates for highway
projects was also considered;
(c) if so, the projects that are being
delayed due to want  of funds  and to what
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

51
extent Government has agreed to provide
funds to these projects;
(d) by what time they are likely to be
completed;
(e) whether  National Highways
Authority of India  has agreed to abandon
two projects at Vijayawada and
Machilipatnam; and
(f) if so, the  reasons therefor?
